subjective.citation_text: Doctor: Hello. Could you tell me your age and gender, and what brings you in today? Patient: I'm 76 years old, and I'm a female. I'm here to establish care with you because I had a lumpectomy last year for ductal carcinoma in situ in my right breast. I'm feeling good overall, but I want to make sure I'm being properly followed up on. Doctor: Could you please provide your height, weight, and any current medications or supplements you are taking? Patient: I'm 76 years old, and I'm a female. I'm here to establish care with you because I had a lumpectomy last year for ductal carcinoma in situ in my right breast. I'm feeling good overall, but I want to make sure I'm being properly followed up on. Doctor: Could you please provide details about your current medications, supplements, and any symptoms or concerns related to your past history of ductal carcinoma in situ? Patient: I take coq10, vitamin d, vitamin c, fish oil, and elderberry fruit. I don't have any symptoms related to my past history, and I'm feeling good overall. I do have some back and knee pain, which my doctors say is age-related, and I've been working on lowering my cholesterol through diet and exercise. Doctor: Please describe the nature, duration, and severity of your back and knee pain, including any factors that aggravate or relieve it. Patient: The back pain is more of a constant ache, especially in the lower back, and it's been going on for a few years. It gets worse when I stand for long periods or lift things, but it feels a little better when I rest or stretch. The knee pain is similar—mostly in my left knee, and it bothers me when I walk or go up stairs, but I can manage it with some rest. Doctor: Could you please provide the results of any recent imaging or laboratory tests related to your breast cancer follow-up or the back and knee pain
